proposals: The Bureau of Indian Standards should publish a draft specification for isobutanol–diesel blends before the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas notifies any mandate, so that a 15% blend does not reach pumps without the kind of finished-fuel standard that E20 and CBG already have.

The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas should publish ARAI test results for isobutanol–diesel at the proposed 15% blend, by vehicle type, before notification, so that the mileage cost is measured rather than projected from pilot trials at 2–5% reported only in the trade press.

The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas should publish an official estimate of E20’s mileage loss and its annual cost to drivers, split between E20-compliant and older vehicles, so that the 2–6% penalty paid in mileage rather than at the pump is stated by government, not reconstructed by independent models.

PNGRB should require city-gas distribution entities to report the actual monthly share of CBG in their CNG and PNG sales against the 1%-to-5% obligation, so that compliance with a blend that consumers cannot detect is visible to them in published numbers.

The Ministry of Civil Aviation should publish the average price paid for SAF and the conventional ATF benchmark each year once the 1% mandate starts in 2027, so that the premium is reported on one consistent India basis instead of per-tonne spot prices and per-litre projections.
